I've got the full picture across the stack. Here's the review of the handoff process and its verdicts.

## What the handoff is

`.drain-handoff.json` is the **exit record a stack-mode worker leaves behind** for the orchestrator to read after the worker finishes an issue. It's the one file the supervisor reads to answer three questions on every exit path (Done, halted, or errored):

1. Did the worker actually submit PRs? (`pr_urls`)
2. How did the work self-assess? (`outcome_verdict`, `prep_verdict`) — schema v2
3. If it didn't reach Done, what verdicts did it manage to record before stopping?

The module is `drain_cycle/handoff.py`. Note a division of labour: the **`/shape:pr-finishing` skill writes the JSON** (it owns `gt`/`gh` and the file); the Python `write()` is the canonical serializer/test helper. The **orchestrator only reads** — it's the sole reader of `pr_urls`.

## The API

Three functions and two dataclasses:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PullRequest:
    title: str
    url: str

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HandoffData:
    pr_urls: tuple[PullRequest, ...]
    outcome_verdict: dict | None = None   # the outcome verifier's self-assessment
    prep_verdict: dict | None = None      # the PR-prep routing decision

write(worktree: Path, data: HandoffData) -> None
read(worktree: Path) -> HandoffData | None                       # strict: gated on valid pr_urls
read_partial(worktree: Path) -> tuple[dict|None, dict|None]      # lenient: verdicts only, no gate
```

**The key design decision is two readers with different strictness:**

- **`read`** is the *confirmation signal*. It returns `None` unless `pr_urls` is a non-empty list of well-formed `{title, url}` entries. A present-but-empty list reads as `None` on purpose — the skill writes URLs only *after* a PR is created, so "empty" means submission never happened. The orchestrator uses this to decide whether the per-repo chain may continue or must halt.
- **`read_partial`** skips the `pr_urls` gate entirely and pulls just the two verdicts. This is what the **halt and breach paths** use — when a worker dies before submitting, there are no PRs, but it may still have written a `fail` verdict explaining why. `read_partial` carries that into the run log so the halt is inspectable.

Both reads are crash-proof: missing file, truncated JSON, or wrong shape all return `None`/`(None, None)` rather than raising.

### Example: the happy-path round trip

```python
from pathlib import Path
from drain_cycle.handoff import HandoffData, PullRequest, read, write

# Worker side (conceptually — the pr-finishing skill does this):
data = HandoffData(
    pr_urls=(
        PullRequest(title="feat: crash-proof filter", url="https://github.com/o/r/pull/1"),
        PullRequest(title="feat: transcript core",    url="https://github.com/o/r/pull/2"),
    ),
    outcome_verdict={"result": "pass", "findings": [], "invoked_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
    prep_verdict={"result": "ok", "route": "auto-merge", "reasoning": "looks good"},
)
write(worktree, data)

# Orchestrator side:
submitted = read(worktree)
if submitted is None:
    halt("no PR submission — chain stops here")
else:
    for pr in submitted.pr_urls:
        print(pr.title, pr.url)
    landed_in_run_log(submitted.outcome_verdict, submitted.prep_verdict)
```

### How the orchestrator wires it in

The verdict fields are what tie the stack together:

- **PR #22** added `outcome_verdict`/`prep_verdict` to the schema and lands them in the run-log entry on every exit path. The orchestrator prefers an in-memory verdict but falls back to `read_partial` for whatever the worker wrote to disk.
- **PR #23** added `kr2_check.py`: a CI-style gate asserting that **every `Done` run-log entry carries both verdicts** (a Done entry with null verdicts is ungradeable). Non-Done entries are allowed null verdicts because `halt_reason` explains them.
- **PRs #24–28** use the verdicts to drive *recovery*: a `fail` outcome_verdict (or Done-but-no-`pr_urls`) triggers the orchestrator to spawn a finishing sub-agent, which re-runs `/shape:pr-finishing` and writes fresh `pr_urls` + verdicts back; the orchestrator re-reads via `read`/`read_partial`.

The verdict shapes used downstream: `outcome_verdict.result` ∈ `{pass, fail}`; `prep_verdict` carries `{result, route, reasoning}` where `route` ∈ `{auto-merge, human-review}`.

## The tests, in plain English

`tests/test_handoff.py` is essentially a contract spec. The guiding rule: **`read` must never raise — anything wrong returns `None`.**

### Happy path

- **Round-trips** — write a `HandoffData` with two PRs, read it back, get the same PRs. (The basic "it works" test.)
- **Writes to the expected path** — `write` actually creates `.drain-handoff.json` in the worktree.
- **Verdicts round-trip** — write with an `outcome_verdict` and `prep_verdict`, read them back unchanged.
- **Verdicts are optional** — write *without* verdicts, read back, both come out `None`. (A worker that only submitted PRs is still valid.)
- **`read_partial` reads verdicts from a complete handoff** — given a fully-written file, partial-read pulls the verdicts (and returns `None` for one that wasn't set).
- **`read_partial` works with no `pr_urls` at all** — a file containing *only* verdicts (the halt-path case) still yields both verdicts. This is the whole reason `read_partial` exists.

### Failure modes (all return `None` / `(None, None)` instead of crashing)

These describe every way a handoff file can be wrong and prove none of them blow up the orchestrator:

| Scenario | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **File doesn't exist** | Worker never wrote one → "not submitted yet" |
| **Empty file** | Truncated/interrupted write mid-flight |
| **Malformed JSON** (`not valid json{{{`) | Corrupted/partial write |
| **Top level isn't a dict** (`[1,2,3]`) | Wrong shape entirely |
| **No `pr_urls` key** | Some other JSON got written |
| **`pr_urls` is empty `[]`** | The critical one: skill ran but submitted nothing → treated as failure, *not* success |
| **`pr_urls` isn't a list** (a dict) | Shape violation |
| **An entry isn't a dict** (a bare string) | Malformed list element |
| **Entry missing `url`** | Incomplete PR record |
| **Entry has empty `url`** (`""`) | Present but useless |
| **Entry `title` isn't a string** (`42`) | Type violation |
| **Verdict isn't a dict** (a string / `42`) | `read` still succeeds on valid `pr_urls`, just drops the bad verdict to `None` — a garbage verdict can't poison a valid submission |
| **`read_partial` on missing / malformed / non-dict file** | Halt path still gets a clean `(None, None)` |

The semantic spine of the suite is the **empty-`pr_urls`-reads-as-`None`** test — it's what makes "the skill ran but no PR came out" a halt condition rather than a silent pass, which (per your stack-PR-submission-regression memory) was exactly the #14 regression this work fixes.

One note worth flagging for your review: `test_handoff.py` covers the file contract thoroughly, but the *recovery* behaviour (spawn finishing sub-agent on `fail`/no-`pr_urls`, re-read, propagate verdicts) lives in the orchestrator and is covered by separate tests added in PRs #27/#28 — want me to give the same human-friendly walkthrough of those finishing-recovery tests next?
